issues.quote: The regulator on the wall had stopped.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the regulator or any stopped clock.
issues.misreading: A solver could read a stopped regulator as a time-of-death or tampering clue, implying a reading the sheet does not give.

issues.quote: His repeater was in his hand.
issues.fact: The sheet mentions no watch of the master's and no reading from it.
issues.misreading: A repeater is a watch that chimes the time, so a solver could treat it as a source of a clock reading or as a time-of-death clue the sheet does not supply.

issues.fact: The sheet gives no information about the body's temperature or time since death.
issues.misreading: A solver could read the cold hand as a hint about how long the man had been dead, a duration the sheet does not give.

issues.quote: That old Morbier, it strikes by its own face. You can hear it all through the house.
issues.fact: The sheet only says the hall clock struck eleven when the kitchen clock showed three minutes past eleven. It says nothing about how the hall clock's face or sound works, or where it can be heard from.
issues.misreading: The added claims about the clock's face and audibility could be taken as hints about whether the hall clock is accurate or where Rosa was when she heard it.
